leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members prefer B037 as a single prize part naming Craig M. Crews, Raymond J. Deshaies and Hiroshi Handa. All four describe the same design strand (heterobifunctional PROTACs, induced proximity to an E3 ligase) and a mechanistic strand (cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining molecular glues). All four also concede that no PROTAC is yet approved and that the trio leaves out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim. They differ in citation wording: Chabes frames the PROTAC concept through the cereblon mechanism as one idea, Linke and Somfai name both strands, and Sparr names the cereblon-based glue mechanism as a separate and decisive discovery. They also differ in how much weight the clinical gap should carry. Somfai names B005 as the safer choice if the timing is judged early. Chabes, Linke and Sparr do not state a threshold for that judgement. Chabes and Somfai give the opening-ballot count differently (all eight ranked it, six in the top three, versus seven in the top five); both are consistent with the shortlist record.

Two members prefer B005 as a single part for Stephen L. Buchwald and John F. Hartwig, citing about 25 to 30 years of independent confirmation, industrial use and the cleanest two-person credit on the shortlist other than B016. Both flag the same two weaknesses: overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the unresolved Kosugi and Migita precursor question. Brzezinski adds that Hartwig appears on another candidate. Zou stresses that B037 may be more transformative. Brzezinski holds his ordering open depending on whether B037 or B002 become cleaner on attribution.

One member prefers B016 as a single prize part for Roberto Car and Michele Parrinello, on the grounds of a sharply bounded 1985 invention, a two-name credit trail and four decades of maturity. He acknowledges that no one else prefers it, that DFT (1998) and multiscale modelling (2013) may count against another computational prize, and that Parrinello's later work (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials) raises a citation-scope question. He raises a possible B016 plus B060 (Liu) pairing.

One member prefers a two-part configuration: B002 for Peter G. Schultz and Jason W. Chin, and B060 for David R. Liu, three laureates in all. This is the only configuration in the eight files with more than one part. The member acknowledges that the B002 cut omits Lei Wang, Ryan A. Mehl and Shigeyuki Yokoyama, that B060 sits near the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Nishida and Kondo parallel report, and that two chemical-biology parts may look uniform. B037 and B005 are named as alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members state no specific disqualifying conflict for their preferred configuration, and none proposes recusal.

Every member who discusses B037 accepts that it is a genuine chemical idea (induced proximity to the ubiquitin system) with wide independent reproduction, and that the cereblon finding explained thalidomide action.

B037, B005 and B016 recur as alternatives across members: B037 is an alternative for aili-daniel, aqvist-johan and zou-xiaodong, B005 for aili-daniel, aqvist-johan, chabes-andrei and somfai-peter, and B016 for brzezinski-peter and linke-heiner.

Members who prefer B037 and members who prefer other candidates all say that credit assignment and the absence of an approved PROTAC are the main costs of B037, and that B005 is the best-attributed, most mature alternative that the committee has identified besides B016.
B016 and B005 are described by their proponents and by other members as having the cleanest attribution on the shortlist.
scientific_disputes: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one coherent achievement (induced proximity to an E3 ligase) or two discoveries with separate logic and history. Chabes treats them as one idea, while Somfai, Sparr and Chabes also list a split into two parts as an open question, and Aili describes the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism as different discoveries.

Whether C-N coupling (B005) is a conceptually new step or an extension of the Pd cross-coupling logic honoured in 2010. Brzezinski and Zou hold the first view; Aili's response to Brzezinski and the caveats from Brzezinski, Zou and Somfai place the question open.

Whether a methods and theory prize (B016, B005) or a chemical-biology prize (B037, B002 with B060) best serves the Chemistry prize now. Sparr notes that B037 could be read as drug modality rather than chemistry, while Aili sees the chemical-biology inventions as having more direct reach into experimental chemistry and medicine.

Whether base editing (B060) is chemistry in substance (Aili, Chabes: engineered deaminases make a defined chemical change in DNA) and sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize (Aili and Chabes raise this; Chabes ranks B060 as an alternative).
attribution_disputes: B037: eight names are credited and every trio proposed (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) leaves out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim. Specifically unresolved: whether Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex cooperativity) or Sakamoto (co-inventor of the first PROTAC) should replace Deshaies or Handa, as raised by Linke, Somfai, Sparr and Chabes. Sparr moved from Ciulli to Handa as third name after reading the openings.
B037: all four supporters name the same trio, but they word the citation differently, so the question of what the three names are credited for is not identical across them.
B005: whether Kosugi's tin-amide work and Migita's precedent should be reflected in a two-person Buchwald and Hartwig citation (Brzezinski, Zou).

B002: whether Lei Wang, Ryan A. Mehl or Shigeyuki Yokoyama should be credited beside Schultz and Chin (Aili). Only Aili proposes B002 in the preferred configuration; Brzezinski and Zou list it as an alternative.
B060: whether the Nishida and Kondo parallel report weakens a Liu-alone framing (Aili, Chabes).
B016: whether a citation tied to the 1985 invention should mention Parrinello's later methods (Aqvist).
maturity_disputes: B037: no PROTAC is yet an approved drug, according to the four B037 supporters and to Aili. Members differ on whether this is a real maturity problem or a clinical lag, and on whether the settled clinical benefit rests on thalidomide-class glues that were found serendipitously and explained later (Linke, Somfai). Aili notes a first regulatory approval before the decision could change the argument.
B005 and B016 are described as fully mature with decades of independent use; Somfai, Aili, Brzezinski and Zou use this to argue that B005 is the safer fallback if B037 is judged early.
B060: about ten years of independent validation but a clinical safety record still accumulating (Aili, Chabes).
B024: Sparr now regards its maturity concerns as weightier than in her opening ranking and asks whether in vivo evidence will accumulate.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Peter Brzezinski discloses that he is a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou and serves as Secretary and Nobel Foundation board deputy. No shortlisted candidate is from his institution or a collaborator.
Xiaodong Zou discloses her Stockholm University tie to Peter Brzezinski. She notes that Brzezinski is a committee peer and not a candidate.

Heiner Linke (chair) and Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr are all Lund University colleagues, disclosed by all three as an institutional tie to other committee members and with no documented tie to any credited candidate. Linke also notes that Parrinello, Car and nanopore candidates are closer to his own field.
Johan Aqvist notes subject-closeness to B016 (molecular simulation) and his postdoctoral EVB collaboration with Arieh Warshel, who is not credited on any shortlisted ballot.

Daniel Aili notes research overlap with B024 (peptide self-assembly and condensed phases), which he does not propose. Andrei Chabes notes topical overlap with B060 and B024. Emma Sparr notes scientific proximity to B055 and B024, which are alternatives. None states a personal or institutional tie to any credited person.
questions_for_round2: B037: Should the prize part be built on PROTACs, on molecular glues, or on both? If both, can a three-name trio be justified against the eight credited, and does Ciulli or Sakamoto displace Handa or Deshaies?

B037: Is the absence of an approved PROTAC drug a disqualifying maturity problem, a timing risk to be accepted, or irrelevant given approved glue degraders? What evidence would shift each member's view?
If B037 is judged early or too hard to attribute, is B005 the committee's fallback, and does the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize or the Kosugi and Migita precursor question change that?
Can B016 gain support beyond its one proponent, given that only four members ranked it in the opening round and DFT (1998) and multiscale modelling (2013) have already been recognised?

Does the committee want a single-part prize or a two- or three-part configuration, and if so, which pairings fit the three-laureate limit (B002 with B060, as Aili proposes, or B016 with B060, as Aqvist suggests)?
For B002 and B060: does the committee accept the cut that omits Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama, and is base editing distinct enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize to treat as chemistry here?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows four members on B037, two on B005, one on B016 and one on a B002 plus B060 configuration. B037 is the plurality position but not a majority: five votes are needed and four members explicitly prefer it. Its supporters are open about its two weaknesses, attribution and the absence of an approved PROTAC. Members who prefer other candidates name B037 or B005 as their alternatives, so the main question for round 2 appears to be whether the attribution and maturity concerns about B037 are resolvable, and if not, whether B005 is the better prize. The chair's own first preference is B037, and his statement should be weighed as one of the four.
